cost_model.turn_cost: interactive cache_read 773,440,403 / 3,989 messages = 193,893 tokens per extra sequential tool turn; weighted 0.1 (cache-read price) = 19,389
cost_model.result_multiplier: 3: a result token is paid once when produced plus re-read ~20 later turns at 0.1 weight (assumption; the digest has no per-result position)
cost_model.saving_formula: tokens_saved_per_use = removed_result_tokens x 3 + removed_turns x 19,389 - added_tokens x 3

proposals.name: file-map
proposals.summary: A generated, gitignored index of every tracked file with its line count, token estimate and top-level headings or definitions, so agents look paths up instead of exploring with ls/find.
proposals.replaces: Exploratory directory listing before reading: 133 ls (B2), 91 find (B5) and 10 git ls-files (B37) calls, often followed by a Read (S19 Read->ls 10, S23 find->Read 9, S24 ls->Read 9) and wc for sizes (B20).
proposals.trigger: shared-file: regenerated by `python3 workspace/scripts/file_map.py` at session start (SessionStart hook) and after any commit that adds, moves or deletes files; agents read it before running ls/find.
proposals.input: Generator: `file_map.py --root <project root> --out workspace/shared/file-map.md [--exclude <glob>]...`; file list comes from `git ls-files` (subprocess); exclude globs also read from icm-project/file-map.exclude if present.
proposals.output: workspace/shared/file-map.md: one Markdown table per top-level directory with columns path | lines (int) | est_tokens (int, bytes/4) | outline (first 5 Markdown headings or top-level def/class/function names, `; `-separated); rows sorted by path; exit 0, or exit 1 if not inside a git work tree.
proposals.estimate_basis: B2+B5+B37 = 234 calls, 34,107 result tokens (avg 146). Assume 1/3 avoidable = 78 per 9 days x 0.778 = 60/week. Per use: 146 x 3 = 437 result + 0.5 turn x 19,389 = 9,694; minus map load 4,000 tok x 3 = 12,000 per session / (60 uses / 8.6 sessions per week = 7 per session) = 1,714. Net 437 + 9,694 - 1,714 = 8,417 ~ 8,400.
proposals.test_plan: Temp git repo with a .md (3 headings), a .py (2 defs) and an untracked file: map lists exactly the 2 tracked files sorted, with correct line counts, bytes/4 token estimates and outlines; --exclude drops a path; running twice gives byte-identical output; running outside a git repo exits 1.
proposals.risks: A stale map hides new files; mitigate by printing the generating commit SHA in the header and regenerating on SessionStart. The map is project content, so it is gitignored and never enters the shared subtree.

proposals.name: reread-guard
proposals.summary: Blocks a Read of a file whose content and requested range are unchanged since the same session already read it, and says so in one line.
proposals.replaces: Re-reading the same file in one session: 167 reads of 25 files in 67 file-session pairs, so 100 within-session repeats (R1-R25), up to 9 reads of one file in one session (R2, R8, R11).
proposals.trigger: PreToolUse:Read. State is cleared by the same script on SessionStart (source=compact or clear) and PreCompact, because content is no longer in context after compaction.
proposals.input: Hook JSON on stdin: session_id (str), tool_input.file_path (str), tool_input.offset (int|null), tool_input.limit (int|null). State file ${TMPDIR}/icm-reread/<session_id>.json mapping path -> [{sha256, offset, limit}].
proposals.output: Unchanged file and a covered range already read: stdout JSON {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "deny", "permissionDecisionReason": "<path> unchanged since your earlier Read in this session (sha256 <8 hex>); use that content or pass a new offset/limit"}}, exit 0. Otherwise records {sha256, offset, limit} and prints nothing, exit 0.
proposals.estimate_basis: R1-R25: 281,631 tokens / 167 reads = 1,686 avg; 167 - 67 file-session pairs = 100 repeats per 9 days. Assume 40% are unchanged full re-reads (rest follow an Edit or read a new range) = 40 x 0.778 = 31/week. Per use 1,686 x 3 = 5,058 - 60 tok deny message x 3 = 180 -> 4,878 ~ 4,800.
proposals.test_plan: Same file twice with no change -> second call denied; file modified between reads -> allowed; second read with a different offset -> allowed; after a PreCompact event for the session -> allowed; missing file_path or unreadable file -> allowed with exit 0 (fail open).
proposals.risks: The agent may truly need the text again after context was summarised; the compact reset and the explicit 'pass a new offset/limit' escape cover this. Fails open on any error so it cannot block work.

proposals.name: section
proposals.summary: Prints a file's heading or definition outline with line ranges, or just the enclosing section or function around a line number, heading or regex match, in one call.
proposals.replaces: Locate-then-print chains: grep for a line number then sed -n a range (S14 13, S18 10, S22 9), grep then a whole-file Read (S7 18); 113 sed calls (B4) and 323 grep calls (B1).
proposals.trigger: tool: when an agent needs one part of a Markdown, Python, C or C++ file, instead of grep followed by sed or Read.
proposals.input: `section.py <file> --outline` | `section.py <file> --heading <text>` | `section.py <file> --line <int>` | `section.py <file> --match <regex> [--max <int>, default 3]`. Language chosen by extension: .md headings, .py def/class, .c/.h/.cpp/.hpp top-level brace blocks.
proposals.output: --outline: lines `<start>-<end> <level> <title>`; other modes: for each hit, a header line `== <file>:<start>-<end> <title>` followed by the numbered lines of that section, at most 400 lines per section with a `... truncated at <n>` marker. Exit 0 on a hit, 1 when nothing matches, 2 for an unsupported extension or unreadable file.
proposals.estimate_basis: S14+S18+S22+S7 = 50 chains per 9 days x 0.778 = 39/week; assume half collapse into one call = 19/week. Each collapsed chain removes one sequential turn = 19,389; result size taken as unchanged (sed avg 45,234/113 = 400 tok) -> ~19,000.
proposals.test_plan: Fixtures: .md with nested headings, .py with nested defs, .c with two functions. --outline ranges match hand-computed values; --line inside the second C function prints exactly that function; --heading picks the right nested section; --match with 5 hits and --max 3 prints 3; no match exits 1; .bin exits 2.
proposals.risks: Brace matching in C can be fooled by braces in strings, comments or macros; strip comments and string literals before counting and print the raw lines. Truncation could hide text, so the marker states the full range.

proposals.name: repo-state
proposals.summary: One call that prints branch, upstream ahead/behind, short status, stash count, the last N commits and a diff stat.
proposals.replaces: Separate git status (B6 66), git log (B7 62) and git branch (B21 19) calls, often spread over several turns before commits and PRs.
proposals.trigger: tool: before committing, branching, opening a PR or reporting work state, instead of separate git status/log/branch calls.
proposals.input: `repo_state.py [--log <int>, default 5] [--base <ref>, default the upstream or main] [--json]`; runs git subprocesses in the current work tree.
proposals.output: Plain text (or with --json an object {"branch": str, "upstream": str|null, "ahead": int, "behind": int, "status": [["XY", "path"]], "stashes": int, "log": [["sha7", "subject"]], "diffstat": {"files": int, "insertions": int, "deletions": int}}); exit 0, or exit 1 outside a git work tree.
proposals.estimate_basis: B6+B7+B21 = 147 calls, 13,609 tok; assume ~2.5 calls per state check = 59 checks per 9 days x 0.778 = 45/week. No git pair appears in the top sequences, so most calls are parallel: assume 0.3 turns saved x 19,389 = 5,817; result size about equal -> ~5,800.
proposals.test_plan: Temp repo with an upstream clone: one commit ahead, one modified and one untracked file, one stash -> JSON fields equal those values; --log 2 gives 2 entries; detached HEAD gives branch "HEAD" and upstream null; run outside a repo exits 1.
proposals.risks: Hides git's advice text (e.g. merge-in-progress). Include a `state` field set from .git/MERGE_HEAD, REBASE_HEAD and CHERRY_PICK_HEAD so unusual states stay visible.

proposals.name: edit-context
proposals.summary: After an Edit, adds the edited region with 3 lines of context and line numbers to the conversation so the agent does not Read the file again to check it.
proposals.replaces: Read immediately after Edit to verify the change: S5 Edit->Read 23, S10 Edit,Edit,Read 16, S11 Edit,Read,Edit 15, out of 312 Edits (T3).
proposals.input: Hook JSON on stdin: tool_input.file_path (str), tool_input.new_string (str), tool_input.replace_all (bool). Reads the edited file from disk after the edit.
proposals.output: stdout JSON {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PostToolUse", "additionalContext": "<path>:<start>-<end>\n<numbered lines>"}} for the first occurrence of new_string plus 3 lines either side, at most 40 lines; prints nothing when new_string is not found or is empty; always exit 0.
proposals.estimate_basis: T3 312 Edits x 0.778 = 243/week. S5 23 Edit->Read of 312 = 7.4%; assume half stop re-reading. Saving per Edit = 0.074 x 0.5 x (19,389 turn + 1,525 avg Read [T2 547,590/359] x 3) = 0.037 x 23,964 = 884; minus added context 150 tok x 3 = 450 -> 434 ~ 430.
proposals.test_plan: Edit fixture replacing one line in the middle of a 100-line file -> context shows that line with 3 lines each side and correct numbers; edit at line 1 clips at file start; 80-line new_string is capped at 40 lines; deletion (empty new_string) prints nothing; non-existent path exits 0 with no output.
proposals.risks: Adds tokens to every Edit; if agents keep re-reading anyway it is a net loss. Measure S5 in the next digest and remove the hook if the Edit->Read rate does not fall by half.

proposals.name: test-summary
proposals.summary: Runs a test command and prints only counts, duration and the first failure excerpts.
proposals.replaces: Full pytest (B14 29 calls, 33,887 tok) and unittest (B17 22 calls, 14,982 tok) output in the main context, up to 6,306 tok in one result (L14).
proposals.trigger: tool: whenever an agent or build-runner runs a test command from icm-project/build.md.
proposals.input: `test_summary.py [--max-failures <int>, default 3] [--excerpt-lines <int>, default 30] -- <test command...>`; runner type (pytest, unittest, ctest) detected from argv[0..2]; the full log is written to ${TMPDIR}/icm-test-<unix time>.log.
proposals.output: First line `PASS|FAIL <runner> passed=<int> failed=<int> errors=<int> skipped=<int> time=<float>s log=<path>`, then per failing test a `--- <test id>` header and at most --excerpt-lines lines of its traceback; exit code equals the wrapped command's exit code.
proposals.estimate_basis: B14+B17 = 51 calls, 48,869 tok, avg 958 per run. Summary ~150 tok. (958 - 150) x 3 = 2,424 ~ 2,400. 51 per 9 days x 0.778 = 39/week.
proposals.test_plan: Fixture unittest and pytest suites with 3 passing and 2 failing tests: header counts are 3/2, two failure blocks, exit code non-zero; all-pass suite prints one line and exits 0; --max-failures 1 prints one block; a command that is not found exits 127 with the header marked FAIL errors=1.
proposals.risks: Counts parsed from runner output can break on format changes; if parsing fails, fall back to printing the last 40 lines of the log. The full log path is always printed.

proposals.name: grep-cap
proposals.summary: Rewrites recursive grep/rg Bash commands that have no -l, -c, -m or pipe so their output is capped at 60 lines plus a per-file match count.
proposals.replaces: Unbounded recursive grep through Bash: 323 calls, 121,494 result tokens (B1), repeated grep->grep refinements (S13 13).
proposals.input: Hook JSON on stdin: tool_input.command (str). Applies only when the command is a single grep -r/-R or rg invocation (shlex-parsed, no |, ;, && or >) without -l, -c, -m, --count or --files-with-matches.
proposals.output: When it applies, stdout JSON {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "allow", "updatedInput": {"command": "<original> | python3 workspace/hooks/grep_cap.py --tail 60"}}}, where --tail mode prints the first 60 lines then `[grep-cap] <n> more lines; matches per file: <path>=<count>, ...`. Otherwise prints nothing; always exit 0.
proposals.estimate_basis: B1 323 calls, avg 376 tok. Assume 10% (32 calls per 9 days) exceed 60 lines by ~1,500 tok -> 32 x 0.778 = 25/week. Per use 1,500 x 3 = 4,500 minus 10% needing a narrower rerun x 19,389 = 1,939 -> 2,561 ~ 2,500.
proposals.test_plan: `grep -rn foo .` is rewritten; `grep -rl foo .`, `grep foo file`, `grep -rn foo . | head` are untouched; --tail mode on 100 input lines prints 60 lines plus a summary with correct per-file counts; on 10 lines it prints them unchanged with no summary; grep exit status 1 (no match) is preserved.
proposals.risks: Silent truncation could hide the one needed match; the summary lists per-file counts so the agent can narrow. Rewriting commands the user approved could surprise them, so the rewrite is visible in the transcript and limited to read-only grep/rg.

proposals.name: read-size-guard
proposals.summary: Caps a Read of a large file without offset/limit to its first 200 lines and adds the file's heading outline with line ranges.
proposals.replaces: Whole-file Reads of large documents and tests: 12 Read results between 5,907 and 13,643 tokens (L1-L11, L15), e.g. long reference documents.
proposals.input: Hook JSON on stdin: tool_input.file_path (str), tool_input.offset (int|null), tool_input.limit (int|null). Applies when offset and limit are both null and file size / 4 > 4,000 tokens (threshold overridable by ICM_READ_CAP_TOKENS env var).
proposals.output: When it applies, stdout JSON {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "allow", "updatedInput": {"file_path": <same>, "limit": 200}, "additionalContext": "<path> is ~<n> tokens; showing lines 1-200. Outline:\n<start>-<end> <heading>..."}}, outline from P3's --outline function; otherwise prints nothing; always exit 0.
proposals.estimate_basis: L1-L11 + L15 = 111,700 tok over 12 reads = 9,308 avg; 12 per 9 days x 0.778 = 9/week (lower bound: only the top 15 results are listed). Capped read 2,000 + outline 600 = 2,600; (9,308 - 2,600) x 3 = 20,124; minus 50% needing a follow-up section read x (2,500 x 3 + 19,389) = 13,445 -> 6,679 ~ 6,600.
proposals.test_plan: 20,000-byte Markdown file with 6 headings read without limit -> updatedInput.limit is 200 and the outline lists 6 ranges; same file with offset set -> no output; 8,000-byte file -> no output; env var 1000 lowers the threshold; binary or missing file -> no output, exit 0.
proposals.risks: The needed text may be past line 200; the outline gives exact ranges for a follow-up Read. Short-but-critical files are unaffected by the size threshold.

proposals.name: md-table-query
proposals.summary: Selects rows and columns from the Markdown tables in a document by column value, so table-heavy reference documents are queried instead of read whole.
proposals.replaces: Reading a whole large reference document made of tables to find a few rows: table document read 8 times in 3 sessions (R5, 21,131 tok), single reads of 9,610 (L5) and 13,643 tok (L1).
proposals.trigger: tool: when an agent needs specific rows (by id, status or owner) from a Markdown table document.
proposals.input: `md_table.py <file> [--table <int or heading text>] [--where <col>=<regex>]... [--columns <col,col>] [--json]`; column names match header cells case-insensitively.
proposals.output: The matching rows as a Markdown table with the original header (or with --json a list of objects keyed by header), preceded by `# <file> table <n> under "<heading>": <k> of <total> rows`; exit 0 with rows, 1 when no rows match, 2 for an unknown column or table.
proposals.estimate_basis: R5 21,131 tok / 8 reads = 2,641 avg; query result ~300 tok. (2,641 - 300) x 3 = 7,023 ~ 7,000. 8 reads per 9 days x 0.778 = 6/week (L1 and L5 not counted).
proposals.test_plan: Fixture with two tables under different headings, one containing escaped pipes: --where status=open returns the 2 open rows; --table by heading picks the second table; --columns keeps order; escaped | stays in the cell; unknown column exits 2; no match exits 1.
proposals.risks: Prose between rows or cells with line breaks is not returned; the header line reports total rows so the agent knows what was filtered out.

rejected.idea: Model-written summaries of the most re-read authority documents (R4, R12, R13, R17)
rejected.reason: Needs a model to produce the summary: fails the deterministic rule. Subject dossiers and the subject-expert agent already cover this.

rejected.idea: PreToolUse:Agent hook forcing a workspace agent instead of general-purpose (A1 11 spawns, S20/S25)
rejected.reason: The digest has no per-subagent token cost, so no saving can be estimated from its counts; choosing an agent from free-text task descriptions is also not a machine-checkable rule.

rejected.idea: SessionStart hook injecting git status and recent commits (B6, B7)
rejected.reason: Duplicates what exists: the harness already injects a gitStatus snapshot at session start. P4 covers mid-session checks.

rejected.idea: Hook blocking foreground sleep polling (B16 24 calls)
rejected.reason: Duplicates what exists: the harness already blocks foreground sleep; results are 646 tok in total.

rejected.idea: Hook redirecting Bash cat/head/tail of a file to Read (B3, B15, B29)
rejected.reason: Output is the same content either way, so no token saving can be shown; P2, P3 and P8 address the size of reads instead.
23 calls in 2 sessions and 5,041 result tokens in total; too little evidence of repeated URLs to estimate a saving, and results are external content.
Write results are ~42 tok each (T4 4,848/116); the content is model-generated, so no deterministic tool can replace it.
